108.t: Future recording plans, dental trouble and Love Me Tender
108.s: He is unsure about more recording because of dental work affecting his playing, and explains why he recorded Love Me Tender.
108.q: I don’t know, I don’t know. It depends. I’ve had some dental work done and I’m having, I’m not too happy with the results I’m getting with my playing as a result of it, and I have to have some adjustments made and when I go back to New York I’ll see what I can do about it and see if it improves. If…

108.t: Picking and choosing work at an older age
108.s: Wilder says offers are fewer now and playing with the Smithsonian Orchestra demands more effort, but he can decline jobs he would not enjoy.
108.q: I think you’re almost right on that. I think I’m picked and chosen on occasion. I sometimes have the privilege of deciding what I want to do, but the offers are not that numerous now. And you know the other thing is I’m much older and I started out as a young player and some of the older fellows…

108.t: Hopes for noncompetitive playing and church music
108.s: He hopes to play for joy, maybe at the Swedish church.
108.q: No, not really. I would like to be someplace where – I may start playing at the church. I belong to a Lutheran church on Fifth Avenue there, the Swedish church, the Seamens Church. I like the atmosphere there. They have a few other musicians. We were talking more recently about the possibility of…

209.t: Pension and Social Security support his choosiness
209.s: Because his studio work was legitimate, the musicians' pension fund and Social Security leave him comfortable. He still plays weekly with friends.
209.q: Yes, yes. Well we have, the young people don’t really know how valuable it is and that’s why they do a lot of work unreported off the record, for under scale and things. But the musician’s pension fund is a very strong and stable fund, and I happened to be working, and all the work I was doing was…

209.t: Semi-retirement, Japan trips and playing for pleasure
209.s: He is mostly retired, no longer cares about the woodwinds, goes to Japan with bands about yearly and turns down casual dances.
209.q: Well I’m pretty much retired now. I’ve actually gone exactly the opposite direction than I was for those 20 years I was working in the studios. I don’t really care about playing the woodwinds anymore at all. I don’t bother with them unless I know in advance something’s coming up that I want to do…

97.t: Wrap-up: board of directors, no thought of playing again
97.s: Scott says his main interest is the Amsterdam.
97.q: Yes, I think we have. And right now, my main interest is the Amsterdam Club, and I'd like sometime to have you up there when we have a particular night, as a guest, and I'm on the board of directors there now. I didn't want to be on there, but they put me on, they made me get on it.

97.t: Staying in touch with music through the Amsterdam Club
97.s: He cannot play but follows music.
97.q: Well, listen, there's a lot of young musicians coming in. And, yeah, I used to follow the bands as much as I could to see them on the radio or read about them in the papers or books. And then the Amsterdam, you see, that's one organization where we keep in touch with everything that's going on.

241.t: Plans for retirement and work around the house
241.s: He says he will keep going rather than sit down, and talks about getting people to paint his house.
241.q: What I want to do, what you going to do? Just sit there and die, that's what you going to do. That's all you going to do, you know what I mean? Once you sit there, that's it. You know what I mean? So, as long as the man can give you the life and help, keep it going, you know what I mean? Just keep…

855.t: Motivation for playing and current activity; Keith Smith visit
855.s: Playing for joy, practicing at home, and an upcoming street parade with Keith Smith's Climax Jazz Band.
855.ch: Discovering jazz and playing in Berlin
855.q: No, no, it was the joy of this music and playing music. And it was just a pleasure to play music, as we heard it on the plates.

311.t: Health now, his children and modesty
311.s: His health has dipped; he is glad he stayed home to raise four good kids and feels modest about knowing great musicians.
311.q: Well right now, the last year or two I’ve kind of — my health kind of went down a little bit, gee I was very active. But in the last few months I feel little problems. But I try to keep my sense of humor anyway.

407.t: Retirement, age and coaching a protege
407.s: He recalls Jay McShann at Kansas City, doubts he will stop playing, and speaks of grandchildren and coaching.
407.q: I was five years old and he was playing and I’m there, not on the dais but in the broader distinguished people for what it was and I looked him tiptoeing out to the piano smiling, you know balancing on air with his two hands. So I told the boy sitting next to me, I said, “Man when I get so old that…

504.t: Staying calm and playing weekly in retirement
504.s: He says he chose high-level situations and now plays weekly with musicians for fun.
504.q: I was fortunate enough to take situations where that didn’t happen you know. I was always in a situation where I felt that I was at the highest level of creativity and quality so I was fortunate enough to be in those kind of situations. I’d put myself in those situations.

606.s: Ellis says he is blessed with good health, plays about half the time, and would play regardless of money.
606.ch: Pay, health and the Gibson guitar
606.q: They are very good. There is something to be said for playing as long as I have. You know I’m very blessed. The Lord has blessed me. I don’t have arthritis and my health is good, so I play about half the time now. And even if I didn’t have to play financially I’d still play because I love it. It’s…

795.s: Gluck says he seeks less stimulation, recalling a quiet week in Vermont versus New York.
795.q: Yes. I mean I do listen to music. I like to — well let’s put it this way — I was recently, about a week or so ago we were up in Vermont for a week with just the dog and my wife. The kids are at camp. And it’s just delightful up there. And we listened to music in the car but I don’t think I was…

731.t: Playing into old age, Snooky Young and Joe Wilder
731.s: Jenkins expects to keep playing longer than teaching, citing Snooky Young and Joe Wilder, and wants to play newer music as he ages.
731.q: I know. But well we were just talking about Joe Wilder. And I was introduced to him by Snooky Young. And Snooky and I were together in the Clayton-Hamilton band for 26 years. And he lived to be 90. He played until he passed away. And I just saw how young it kept him. And my dad played and it kept…

809.t: Staying in touch with his brothers and retirement
809.s: Weekly Zoom with John and Joe; his retirement plans during Covid.
809.q: We’re all together usually every Sunday around 1:30 and we talk on Zoom. And then we’ll pass on stuff. Or I’ll try to remember — I’ll say do you remember this, or do you remember this happening or that happening. And we’ll pass on information. We’re always talking you know, or texting. No we’re…

582.t: No retirement: musicians who keep playing
582.s: They joke about retirement and cite Moody, Elvin Jones and Milt Hinton as examples of music as a life force.
582.q: What am I going to retire to? What am I going to retire to? That’s the great thing. I mean I look at James Moody, he’s 76. I talked to Pat LaBarbara today, he’s going to go out and play with Elvin again. You know Elvin is 73. These guys are only getting better. What are they going to do go play…

523.s: Raph says he looks to the future, wants to stay active for his daughter, and the interview closes.
523.q: Writing a lot. Actually a large part of my life right now is my ten-year-old. I want to stay around long enough to give her a good shot at life. So the more years I can keep going and staying active in all of that, the better chance she has of relating and learning some

216.t: Retirement, Covid and My Fair Lady
216.s: He keeps busy outdoors, returns to clarinet for a Broadway show of My Fair Lady and helps a friend with a soprano sax piece.
216.q: Oh what I do is, if it’s in the summer I’m working outside a whole lot. I’ve got a chain saw and that kind of thing. But I still, with Covid I thought okay this kind of has stopped

671.s: He is 76, semi-retired, enjoys the Jerome party and left it to the organizer who he plays with.
671.q: Play a little bit, relax, I’m not a great television fan. I like to watch sports and I like to drive my car. You know, nothing — I’m 76 now, and I really am semi-retired.

86.t: Closing: no wish list, takes life as it comes
86.s: He has no further projects in mind and enjoys surprises.
86.q: You know, I’ve never been one to sit and say, well, I hope this happens, I hope I’ll be able to do this, I hope something like this. Because, I just take life as it comes. If it happens, I’m surprised and I love surprises. So, I just take it and enjoy. End of Cd #6

219.t: Learning new media and keeping Newport alive
219.s: Wein talks about learning online promotion and his pro bono work for the Newport foundation.
219.q: I think we can fade. I like to talk but … it's more or less getting your philosophies out there because people don't really know that there is a lot of thinking goes into this type of thing. It's not just that this group will sell and this group will reach these children this way … that's not what…

65.t: Closing: happiness, grandchildren, and no retirement
65.s: At seventy, Machito is happy, hopes his grandchildren do well in music, and has no plans to retire; interview ends.
65.q: Gee, I would like to see my grandchildren to have a good career and make something at it. I am lucky because one of my daughters she send my grandchildren to every school that you can think. I have a five years old

231.t: What he would like to be doing now
231.s: Disabled by his condition, he says he has done enough and would be happy resting.
231.q: think I've done enough, you know. I would lay down now and be peaceful. Then I could do a little of this and a little of that and it would be all right. But a whole lot of this and that, no good. I'm not able.

167.t: Favorite groups: Ink Spots and Lionel Hampton; avoiding public life
167.s: He most enjoyed the Ink Spots and Lionel's group, and stays out of public life because he cannot see well.
167.q: Yeah. Since I stopped going into public life, which I think is best for me right now because I'd be in a whole lot of scrapes and be liable to get hurt because I can't see too much, you know.

120.t: Unissued tapes, retirement and model trains
120.s: He may let Jim Rivers issue his tapes, plans a model railway in retirement, and says he cannot believe he is seventy-four.
120.ch: Looking back and the lean years
120.q: And, uh, that's why I wanted to work out with Jim Rivers; I think if anyone is going to issue that stuff - I think I should let him do it and, uh, oh - say -"the Best of Wild Bill" - to take a lot of things that maybe people haven't heard and make albums and so on. But, that's something I can do…

453.t: Teaching in his senior years and hopes for an opera
453.s: At 78 he prefers to stay teaching rather than tour, comments on Eubie Blake, and asks DeMichael to help find a sponsor for his opera.
453.q: Well, I don't know. I get to thinking, I just want to put some talent out there now, try to see if I can get some people doing some things. Get them to do things that I want them to do. Try to get them to do the things I want them to do. And I want to get this opera going, if I can.

94.s: Moore explains he is semi-retired, staying home and playing occasionally.
94.q: It's only a couple of years. It got to the point where I was more needed around home, and they'll be away because Ida is teaching and the kids are grown up/and Randy is living in Brooklyn and Amy is working and there's nobody to be around home here and I do odds and ends around here like I do a…

149.s: He plans to stay at the Concord and has property in Birmingham.
149.q: Well, I'm not, I don't have too much, nothing else hardly to do this cause I had made my mind up to stay here until I figure I'm ready to sit down and quit and go in. I can't go no further. I'm feeling all right. I feel good. I don't have no other business on the side, you know. So, I go home where…
